findings.title: Wrap before truncating, and never truncate what matters
findings.where: Install section, Claude Code and Codex cards (div.sheet.rise code lines), 1440px, tiles/1440-10.png
findings.evidence: The tile shows '/plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-de' cut at the right edge of the Claude Code card and 'codex plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagr' cut at the right edge of the Codex card, with no ellipsis. The table's long_unbroken_strings rows put the text's right edge on the box's right edge (text_right 939 against box_right 938; 1377 against 1378). The page declares no overflow-wrap rule.
findings.before: Each install command is one unbreakable line that the card cuts at its edge.
findings.after: Let the command lines wrap inside the card (white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere on the code lines), or give the block a visible horizontal scroll.
findings.why: The repository name is the part a visitor must read or retype, and the cut hides it. The COPY button helps only mouse users who trust it blind.

findings.title: Room for other languages

findings.evidence: rows_without_room_for_35pct: five links in a 556px row with free_px 21 against needed_for_35pct_px 169. The stylesheet has no flex-wrap evidence for this row on the tile; the five labels already fill the column.
findings.before: Five uppercase tag links fill their column with 21px to spare.
findings.after: Let the tag row wrap (flex-wrap: wrap with a row gap).
findings.why: The page is English-only, so this is a readiness note: a longer gallery name or a translation will push the last tag out of line.
